dedupe_keys.name: barcelona superblocks green infrastructure and social justice in heat adaptation spain

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes Barcelona's Superblock programme, started in 2015, as a way to expand green infrastructure in one of Europe's densest cities while taking account of social justice. Barcelona covers just over 100 square kilometres with more than 1.6 million people, very little green space and growing heat waves. Superblocks restrict private motor traffic in groups of blocks and turn streets into green, shaded public space, and equity considerations such as the needs of vulnerable groups and the risk of gentrification were built into decision making and participation. Pilots ran in Poblenou from 2016 and in Sant Antoni from 2017 to 2019, and in 2023 the city planned to scale the concept up across the Eixample district; costs vary with the mix of structural, tactical and governance elements. The page is free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal (2025), citing the Barcelona climate plan and Eggimann (2022) in Nature Sustainability. Caveats: outcomes are reported qualitatively, green space gains are local, and gentrification pressure is a known risk. It illustrates policy evaluation of street-scale green infrastructure for heat and equity; a related record is the UN-Habitat open space indicator data.
name: Barcelona Superblocks, green infrastructure and social justice in heat adaptation (Spain)
outcomes: Superblock pilots in Poblenou and Sant Antoni added green, shaded public space and led to plans to scale up across the Eixample district, with equity built into the process.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study on the Barcelona City Council Superblock programme
